name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
summary: An isolation exercise that strengthens the forearm flexors by curling dumbbells upward at the wrists while the forearms remain supported.

setup: Sit on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a supinated (underhand) grip.
Rest your forearms flat along your thighs or across the bench, allowing your wrists and hands to hang off the edge.
steps: Lower the dumbbells as far as comfortable by extending your wrists toward the floor.
Curl your wrists upward as high as possible, contracting the flexor muscles on the underside of your forearms.
Pause briefly at peak contraction before slowly lowering the weights back to the starting stretch.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you curl the dumbbells up; inhale as you lower them into extension.
cues: Keep your forearms glued to the support.
Isolate the movement strictly to your wrists.
Control the descent; do not bounce out of the bottom stretch.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the forearms or elbows off the support to cheat the weight up.
common_faults.correction: Keep your forearms pinned flat against your thighs or the bench throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive momentum and snapping the wrists.
common_faults.correction: Use lighter dumbbells and execute a controlled, deliberate contraction with a brief pause at the top.

precautions: Avoid hyperextending the wrist under excessive load to prevent wrist strain or tendon irritation.
